content.text:
Put it in a **new migration file, `migrations/0008_add_customer_phone.sql`**. Don't edit `0007_add_customers.sql`, even though that's where the `customers` table is created.

The project memory says files in `migrations/` have already been applied in production. Changing one won't affect databases that already ran it, so their schema would drift from the repo. Schema changes go in a new file numbered after the highest one (with 4 digits). That's `0007` now, so the next is `0008`.

```sql
-- migrations/0008_add_customer_phone.sql
ALTER TABLE customers ADD COLUMN phone TEXT;
```

Leave the column nullable, or give it a `DEFAULT`. The table already has rows, and a plain `NOT NULL` column with no default will fail on many databases. If you need `NOT NULL`, backfill the existing rows first and add the constraint in the same migration or a later one.

Also, `0007` misspells the email column as `emial`. If you want to fix that, do it in its own new migration (e.g. `ALTER TABLE customers RENAME COLUMN emial TO email;`) and update any code that uses the column, not by editing `0007`. I didn't find any code under `src/` that uses it right now.
